newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn budget deficit 40 bln DM in Q1 - SPD.
newsitem.headline: Bonn budget deficit 40 bln DM in Q1 - SPD.

text.p: The German government ran up a federal budget deficit in the first three months of 1997 equal to nearly three quarters of the level alloted for the full year, an opposition Social Democrat (SPD) parliamentarian said on Friday.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Finance Minister Theo Waigel continue to say Germany will reduce its budget deficit to three percent of economic output this year to qualify for European monetary union, but scepticism is mounting.

The federal deficit in January to March totaled 39.7 billion marks, compared with a projected full-year deficit of 53.4 billion marks budgeted for the full year, said SPD budget spokesman Karl Diller. Spending was 7.3 percent higher than budgeted while revenues were 9.9 percent lower, he said.
"This is a first in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany," Diller said. "Kohl's chaos cabinet will exceed the year's budget deficit in a few weeks."
Parliament's finance committee will discuss the budget situation with Waigel next Wednesday.

Diller urged Kohl to draw up a supplementary budget, or risk contravening budget law and the constitution, which says the deficit cannot exceed government investment spending, budgeted at 59.6 billion marks this year.
Waigel has often said in the past that short-term budget data are not a reliable indicator of full-year results.
